decision: Q1: extend existing ac-NN convention; splits become ac-NN.M with parent ID preserved
reasoning: verifier.ts:86 already uses ac-01 convention and phase-01 plans used it; zero migration, schema is unconstrained z.string so ac-NN.M parses fine
risk: dotted sub-ids could be misread as decimals by future tooling doing numeric sort

decision: Q2: IDs live in plan-level '## Verification Criteria' section (one ac-NN per line + Anti: entries); per-task Verification lines reference the ac-IDs they satisfy
alternatives: carry ac-IDs directly on per-task Verification lines; duplicate in both places
reasoning: single source of truth for verifier consumption (verifier reads the criteria section), keeps per-task lines lean within 3-sentence budget, avoids drift between two ID lists
risk: indirection: executor must cross-reference section to find probe details

decision: Q3: option (b) — new 'luca plan lint' CLI handler, advisory warn-only, invoked by architect + phase-plan instructions after writing plan.md
alternatives: (a) stage-gate hook content lint at handle-stage-gate-hook.ts:171-217 covering both write paths deterministically; (c) instruction-only with lint as follow-up todo
reasoning: covers dominant native-Write path when instructions invoke it, zero hook latency/false-positive blocking risk, regex checks are deterministic, warn-only is legitimate incremental step per hook/skill boundary; hook enforcement can be promoted later once regexes prove out
risk: instruction-invoked lint can be skipped by a non-compliant agent — enforcement is advisory not deterministic this phase

decision: Q4: keep 150-line budget but exempt the '## Verification Criteria' section from the count; state exemption in same architect.ts edit at :38 and :396
alternatives: raise budget to 200 lines flat; no change (let enumeration squeeze task detail)
reasoning: enumeration + anti-criteria are the new mandated content — exempting them preserves the anti-padding pressure on task prose while never forcing criteria truncation
risk: agents may pad the exempted section; reviewer checklist must watch for criteria bloat

decision: Tombstones: dropped criteria stay in plan.md as '[DROPPED — see decisions <date>]' but are EXCLUDED from verify.json criteria array entirely
alternatives: blocking:false and tombstone note as evidence
reasoning: exclusion keeps aggregateVerificationResults.allCriteriaMet (verification-result.ts:157-159) semantics clean — no fake met:true entries; validate-verification-ref exact-match correctly rejects done-refs to dropped ids, which we document
risk: audit trail of dropped criteria lives only in plan.md, not verify.json

decision: Added optional notes field line to the verify.json template in verifier.ts so the legacy-plan ID-fallback rule has a coherent target field
alternatives: Reference notes field in the rule text only, leaving the JSON template unchanged
reasoning: Task spec says fallback must be noted in verify.json notes; schema already defines notes as optional (packages/luca-core/src/verification/schemas.ts:71), so documenting it in the template is consistent and required no schema edit
risk: None significant; field is optional and already schema-backed

decision: Placed Criteria Quality Rules as a Step 4 subsection immediately after the plan.md template; anti-criteria pinned as anti-NN grammar per orchestrator instruction, superseding plan.md's literal 'Anti:' wording
alternatives: use 'Anti:' entry label as written in plan.md task text
reasoning: grammar belongs adjacent to the template it constrains; orchestrator prompt explicitly mandated anti-NN wording (NOT 'Anti:') and lint regexes key to anti-NN
risk: plan.md task text says 'Anti:' entries; reviewer may flag the wording divergence

decision: plan lint returns isError only for unreadable --file; lint findings always non-error; check-d reported at line 1; quantifier check skips .M sub-criterion lines
alternatives: treat unreadable file as a warning and still exit 0
omit lineno for the file-level anti-criteria warning
apply quantifier check to sub-criterion lines too
reasoning: warn-only contract reads as lint findings never block; an unreadable path is an operational failure matching readJsonPayload precedent; line 1 keeps the plan lint: file:lineno: format uniform; .M lines are already decomposed leaves
risk: caller piping a bad path expects exit 0 unconditionally; line 1 attribution for check-d could mislead a naive parser
reviewHint: confirm warn-only contract scope: should unreadable --file also exit 0?

decision: Placed the new ## Decisions template section after ## Risks & Mitigations as the final plan.md section, with a one-line entry placeholder plus a trailing note that tombstone refs and lint-warning justifications land there
alternatives: embed the note inside the placeholder line instead of a separate sentence
reasoning: Task spec said minimal one-line entries but did not fix the section position; appending at the end keeps existing section ordering untouched (additive-only constraint) and matches how decisions are referenced (tombstones say 'see decisions <date>')
risk: If the linter or another consumer later keys on section ordering, the Decisions-last placement could need adjustment

decision: Sanitize control chars in the whole error-branch message (err.message), not just the interpolated --file path, and generalize the helper to sanitizeControlChars
alternatives: Sanitize only the directly interpolated args.file and leave err.message raw
Strip control chars instead of escaping them as \xNN
reasoning: Node ENOENT messages embed the raw path, so sanitizing only the interpolation would still leak a raw ESC byte and fail ac-18; \xNN escaping preserves diagnosability over silent stripping
risk: Legitimate control characters inside a foreign error message are rendered escaped rather than verbatim — cosmetic only
reviewHint: ac-18 covers both the summary and error branches; err.message sanitization is what makes the error branch pass
